body.p: The Notice dated September 12, 2024 has been carefully reviewed. Claims 1-2, 9, and 16 have been amended. Claims 3-8 and 17-19 have been cancelled. Claims 1-2 and 9-16 are now pending in this application. Favorable consideration and allowance of this application is respectfully requested in light of the following amendments and remarks.
I. Amendment Support

As stated above, claims 1-2, 9, and 16 have been further amended herein. First, independent claims 1 and 16 have been further amended to define that the at least three satellites in the formation each is equipped with a propulsion system and at least one observation antenna for beam-steering operations by the combination of satellites. Basis for this amendment may, for example, be found on page 3, lines 19-27 and page 10, lines 10-14 of the application as filed.

Independent claims 1 and 16 have been further amended to define that the set of satellites further comprises a sensor unit for obtaining radiation sensor data and at least one communication hub satellite provided with a wireless communication link with a ground station and configured to at least one of obtain and receive at least one of sky and earth observation data collected by the at least three satellites in the multi-satellite formation. Independent claims 1 and 16 have been further amended to define that the control system comprises artificial intelligence software and is configured to obtain at least one of space and earth observation data collected by the observation antenna arrays of the satellites in the multi-satellite formation, obtain radiation sensor data from the sensor unit and pre-known knowledge or artificial intelligence from the artificial intelligence software. Basis for these amendments may, for example, be found on page 5, line 30 to page 6, line
6 and page 8, line 16 to page 9, line 12 of the application as filed.

Independent claims 1 and 16 have been further amended to define that the control system is configured to dynamically and continuously change the configuration and shape of the multi- satellite formation for improved tracking and beam steering operations by the combination of satellites by controlling the propulsion system of the satellites in the multi-satellite formation by sending commands to the propulsion systems of the satellites in the multi-satellite formation at least partly based on observation data collected by the observation antenna arrays of the at least three

satellites in the multi-satellite formation, radiation sensor data obtained by the sensor unit of the satellite system and some pre-known knowledge in terms of previously acquired observation data and artificial intelligence obtained from the artificial intelligence software. Basis for his amendment may, for example, be found on page 5, line 30 to page 6, line 6, page 8, line 16 to page 9, line 12 and page 10, lines 10-14 of the application as filed.
II. Patentability of Amended Claims

The Song reference cited in the previous Office Action relates to a spacecraft formation flying system design and control for a mission involving four nanosats in a predetermined formation and moving in similar orbital planes. The nanosats in the predetermined formation may occasionally drift apart.

Song describes a satellite formation with four nanosats where the relative distance between the nanosats can be decreased and increased during along-track and cross-track formations, respectively, via orbit controls in the desired duration. The problem addressed in Song is that nanosats that move along similar orbital planes in a predetermined formation drift apart owing to the difference in orbital drift rate. The drift recovery control can be performed several times because of thrust limitations and control errors. The orbital control for the formation flying system in Song shall maintain the relative distance to prevent the nanosats from passing through each other, see for example column 1 on pages 151 and 152, and the text to Fig.

The Song reference describes two kinds of satellite formations: along-track formation for time and a cross-track formation for spatial. In the along-track formation, the distance between the individual satellites in the formation is thousands of kilometers and it takes three months to collect the information.

The Song article does not mention anything about the nanosats comprising antennas. Furthermore, Song does not mention anything about beam steering operations by the combination of satellites involving the antenna arrays of a plurality of satellites in the multi- satellite formation.
In order to provide for beam steering operations by the combination of satellites

involving the antenna arrays of a plurality of satellites in formation, the satellites in a multi- satellite formation need to comprise an antenna and be located on substantially the same latitude so, even if the nanosats disclosed in Song would comprise antennas, the formation of nanosats as described in the Song reference would not enable any beam steering operations by the combination of satellites involving the antenna arrays of a plurality of satellites in the formation.

Thus, Song does not disclose a formation of satellites with antennas where observation data collected by at least one of the antennas in the formation may be used for improved beam steering operations by the combination of satellites involving the antenna arrays of a plurality of satellites in formation and dynamically changing the formation by changing the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of the antenna arrays of separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation.
Song does not disclose or mention that the set of satellites in the formation further

comprises a sensor unit for obtaining radiation sensor data and at least one communication hub satellite provided with a wireless communication link with a ground station and configured to obtain and/or receive at least one of sky and earth observation data collected by the other satellites in the multi-satellite formation.

In particular, Song does not mention or hint to a satellite system comprising a control system for controlling a propulsion system of the respective satellite in the multi-satellite formation by sending commands for changing the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of the antenna arrays of separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation based on observation data collected by the antennas in the multi-satellite formation, radiation sensor data obtained by a sensor unit of the satellite system and some pre-known knowledge in terms of previously acquired observation data and artificial intelligence obtained from the artificial intelligence software of the control system.

The Stuart reference discloses a spacecraft design for a Satellite Communication System including a hemispherical, high-gain, electronically-steered antenna array (12) that is always pointed toward the Earth (E). The interior of the dome-shaped antenna array (12) is used to store
solar cell panels (16) which unfurl through an opening (15) in a space-facing array (18) when the spacecraft (10) reaches its final orbit.

Stuart fails to remedy at least the above deficiencies of Song. In particular, Stuart dose not disclose a satellite formation comprising at least three satellites each equipped with a propulsion system and at least one observation antenna for beam-steering operations by the combination of satellites or a control system configured to dynamically and continuously change the configuration and shape of the multi-satellite formation for improved tracking and beam steering operations by the combination of satellites by controlling the propulsion system of the satellites in the multi-satellite formation to thereby change at least the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of the observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation for improved tracking and beam steering operations by the combination of satellites.
The Satak reference discloses a space internet network comprising a Satellite

Constellation 401, a plurality of Earth Internet Gateways 402a... 402n and a plurality of User Terminals 403a, 403b, 403c... 403n. The Satellite Constellation 401 comprises a plurality of satellites 401a, 401b... 401n. The Satellite Constellation 401 forms a network in space, that enables communication between the plurality of satellites 401a, 401b... 40 in and the plurality of Earth Internet Gateways 402a... 402n.

Satak discloses a space satellite-based internet network system comprising inter-satellite communication links to cover a large geographical area. The satellites are orbiting the earth. The steerable beam in Satak is a spot beam for communication and not for sensing. A spot beam is a satellite signal that is specially concentrated in power (i.e. sent by a high-gain antenna) so that it will cover only a limited geographic area on earth. Spot beams are used so that only earth stations in a particular intended reception area can properly receive the satellite signal. Spot beams allow satellites to transmit different data signals using the same frequency. Because satellites have a limited number of frequencies to use, the ability to re-use a frequency for different geographical locations (without different data interfering with each other at the receiver) allows for more local channels to be carried, since the same frequency can be used in several regions.

Satak fails to remedy at least the above deficiencies of Song. In particular, Satak does not disclose a satellite formation comprising at least three satellites each equipped with a propulsion system and at least one observation antenna for beam-steering operations by the combination of satellites or a control system configured to dynamically and continuously change the configuration and shape of the multi-satellite formation for improved tracking and beam steering operations by the combination of satellites by controlling the propulsion system of the satellites in the multi-satellite formation to thereby change at least the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of the observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation for improved tracking and beam steering operations by the combination of satellites.
Claim 24 and FIG. la of the Nichols reference discloses an antenna including a first

planar array of antenna elements and one or more side planar arrays of antenna elements, each side array adjacent to the first array and tilted at a predetermined angle relative to the first array. The antenna may also include a plurality of transmit/receive modules, each module coupled to one antenna element. Each transmit/receive module includes phase shifters for varying the relative phases of the antenna elements to form a desired overall beam pattern, and a low noise amplifier and high-power amplifier for amplifying signals received and transmitted by the antenna element, respectively.

Nichols fails to remedy at least the above-underlined deficiencies of Song. In particular, Nichols does not disclose at least three satellites in a formation each equipped with a propulsion system and at least one observation antenna for beam-steering operations by the combination of satellites or a control system configured to dynamically and continuously change the configuration and shape of the multi-satellite formation for improved tracking and beam steering operations by the combination of satellites by controlling the propulsion system of the satellites in the multi-satellite formation to thereby change at least the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of the observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi- satellite formation for improved tracking and beam steering operations by the combination of satellites.
Paragraph [0040] of the cited reference Rettman discloses a hall effect thruster and a gridded ion thruster using electrostatic actuation for changing the movement and direction of a satellite.

Rettman fails to remedy at least the above-underlined deficiencies of Song. In particular, Rettman does not disclose a satellite formation comprising at least three satellites each equipped with a propulsion system and at least one observation antenna for beam-steering operations by the combination of satellites or a control system configured to dynamically and continuously change the configuration and shape of the multi-satellite formation for improved tracking and beam steering operations by the combination of satellites by controlling the propulsion system of the satellites in the multi-satellite formation to thereby change at least the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of the observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation for improved tracking and beam steering operations by the combination of satellites.
FIGS. 1-3 and 6 of the cited reference Viktorovich discloses a spacecraft comprising a radiation sensor.
Viktorovich fails to remedy at least the above-underlined deficiencies of Song. In

particular, Viktorovich does not disclose a satellite formation comprising at least three satellites each equipped with a propulsion system and at least one observation antenna for beam-steering operations by the combination of satellites or a control system configured to dynamically and continuously change the configuration and shape of the multi-satellite formation for improved tracking and beam steering operations by the combination of satellites by controlling the propulsion system of the satellites in the multi-satellite formation to thereby change at least the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of the observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the multi-satellite formation for improved tracking and beam steering operations by the combination of satellites.

Independent claim 1, as amended, distinguishes over Song, and Song in combination with any and all of the other cited references Stuart, Satak, Nichols, Rettman and Viktorovich by defining a satellite system comprising a control system that is configured to control the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in a formation including at least three satellites

p.u: at least partly based on observation data received by the control system from at least one of the observation antenna arrays of at least one of the satellites in the formation.

body.p: In particular, amended claim 1 distinguishes over Song in combination with any of the other cited references by defining a control system configured to control the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the set at least partly based on observation data collected by at least one observation antenna array to thereby change the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of at least two observation antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the formation for improved beam steering operations by the combination of satellites in the formation for the purpose of tracking a moving object whose observation data is currently collected.
Independent claim 16, as amended, distinguishes over Song, and Song in combination

with any and all of the other cited references Stuart, Satak, Nichols, Rettman and Viktorovich, by defining a method for dynamically controlling the configuration and shape of a satellite formation comprising at least three satellites that includes the step of controlling, by the control system, the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the set at least partly based on observation data collected by at least one of the observation antenna arrays of the satellites in the formation and that is received by the control system.

In particular, amended claim 16 distinguishes over Song, and Song in combination with any and all of the other cited references by defining a method including the step of controlling, by the control system, the propulsion system of at least one of the satellites in the set at least partly based on observation data collected by at least one of the observation antenna arrays of the satellites in the formation to thereby change the relative angle directions of the radiation lobes of at least two antenna arrays of at least two separate satellites in the formation for improved beam steering operations by the combination of satellites in the formation involving the antenna arrays of a plurality of satellites in formation for the purpose of tracking a moving object whose observation data is currently collected.
For at least the reasons discussed above, Applicant contends that independent claims 1
and 16 are patentably distinct form the cited prior art. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests allowance of these claims and all claims depending therefrom.
In light of the amendments and remarks above, Applicant believes the application is in condition for allowance.
